definition: Oracle Data Mining (ODM) is an option of Oracle Database Enterprise Edition.
details: It contains several data mining and data analysis algorithms for classification, prediction, regression, associations, feature selection, anomaly detection, feature extraction, and specialized analytics. It provides means for the creation, management and operational deployment of data mining models inside the database environment.

explainer.lead: Oracle Data Mining is an option of Oracle Database Enterprise Edition that brings data mining and analysis algorithms inside the database itself. It matters because models can be built, managed and deployed where the data already lives.

tiers.eli5: Instead of carrying all your data to a separate workshop to be analysed, you do the analysis right in the room where the data is stored.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to create, manage and operationally deploy models covering classification, prediction, regression, associations, feature selection, anomaly detection and feature extraction without leaving the database environment. A pitfall is assuming it replaces general-purpose ML tooling, since it is tied to this database option.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as an option of Oracle Database Enterprise Edition containing algorithms for classification, prediction, regression, associations, feature selection, anomaly detection, feature extraction and specialized analytics, with means to create, manage and deploy models inside the database environment.

explainer.example: A team builds a classification model on stored customer records and deploys it inside the database, so scoring happens in place rather than in an external system.
